The original [BERT4Rec paper](https://arxiv.org/html/1904.06690) already includes last-item-only masking during training to reduce mismatch with appended-mask inference. Its objective averages cross-entropy over masked targets within each sequence. Its “1 mask” ablation supports controlling supervision count, but compares random single-mask BERT4Rec against SASRec; it does not isolate terminal versus random masking. Mask-rate experiments also change both target count and available context, so their gains cannot establish a terminal-supervision effect.

Suggested controls, inferred from these findings: compare exactly one terminal target against exactly one uniformly sampled nonpadding target per sequence, holding user sampling, optimizer updates, architecture, loss and corruption rule fixed. For multi-target comparisons, average losses within each sequence and then across sequences; averaging all batch targets instead weights histories with more masks more heavily. Report supervised-target counts alongside GPU time and updates. Distinguish terminal-position supervision from recency sampling and removal of right context; [Recency Sampling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.02643) explicitly identifies target selection and alignment with next-item prediction as consequential.

For shortcut checks, measure validation HR@10 by training-derived target popularity and history length, and evaluate sensitivity to shuffled histories, removed positional embeddings, and repeated target IDs remaining visible elsewhere in the history. These are proposed diagnostics, not established terminal-mask ablation results. [Debiasing the Cloze Task](https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.09210) establishes exposure bias as a separate concern; terminal masking alone does not establish its removal. Keep the pinned evaluator unchanged and use diagnostic perturbations only as supplementary analyses, without combining scores from separate predictors.
